# `silk/compress/tar`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

Read the members of a tar archive held in memory.

## When to use
Use a [`TarReader`](#TarReader) to unpack a `.tar` file, or a `.tar.gz` file after you decode it with
`silk.compress.inflate`. Open the archive with [`TarReader.open`](#TarReader.impl.open) and call [`TarReader.next`](#TarReader.impl.next)
until it returns none. This module does not write archives and does not decompress.

## Details
The reader understands ustar, GNU, and pax archives: the ustar `prefix` field, GNU long names,
pax `path` records, and base-256 sizes. It does not allocate, and every member it returns
borrows the archive. Each header's checksum is checked. A member's path is checked before the
member is returned: an absolute path, a backslash, or a `..` segment refuses the archive, so a
caller that joins a path to a directory and creates no links never writes outside it. Empty and
`.` segments are allowed, because `tar -C dir .` writes paths such as `./include/x.h`.

## Errors
- [`TarError`](#TarError) from [`TarReader.next`](#TarReader.impl.next) when a header is corrupt, the archive ends inside a
  member, or a path is unsafe.

## Examples
```silk
import silk.compress.tar {TarError, TarKind, TarMember, TarReader}
import silk.core.option {Option}
import silk.core.result {Result}

// Counts the regular files of `archive`, or answers -1 when it is not a valid tar archive.
fn files(archive: &[u8]) -> i32 {
  let mut reader = TarReader.open(archive)
  let mut count = 0
  while true {
    match TarReader.next(&mut reader) {
      Result<Option<TarMember>, TarError>.Success {value} => match move value {
        Option<TarMember>.Some {value: member} => { if member.kind == TarKind.File { count = count + 1 } }
        Option<TarMember>.None => { return count }
      }
      Result<Option<TarMember>, TarError>.Failure {..} => { return -1 }
    }
  }
  return count
}

pub fn main() -> i32 {
  let empty: [u8; 1024] = [0; 1024]
  return files(&empty)
}
```

<a id="TarMember"></a>

## `TarMember`

```silk
pub struct TarMember<'a>
```

One member of a tar archive: its checked path, its kind, and its content.

### Details
The member's path is `prefix/name`, or `name` alone when `prefix` is empty. A GNU long name or a
pax `path` record comes back as `name` with an empty `prefix`. The slices borrow the archive
given to [`TarReader.open`](#TarReader.impl.open).

<a id="TarMember.prefix"></a>

### Field `prefix`

```silk
pub prefix: &'a [u8]
```

The ustar `prefix` field, or empty.

<a id="TarMember.name"></a>

### Field `name`

```silk
pub name: &'a [u8]
```

The rest of the path, without the trailing `/` a directory may carry.

<a id="TarMember.kind"></a>

### Field `kind`


Whether the member is a file, a directory, a link, or something else.

<a id="TarMember.executable"></a>


Whether the member is a file whose mode has an execute permission bit.

<a id="TarMember.link"></a>


<a id="TarMember.content"></a>

<a id="TarReader"></a>

## `TarReader`

```silk
pub struct TarReader<'a>
```

A position in a tar archive held in memory.

### When to use
Make one with [`TarReader.open`](#TarReader.impl.open) and call [`TarReader.next`](#TarReader.impl.next) until it returns none.

### Details
The reader does not allocate and borrows the archive. It stops at the first all-zero block or at
the end of the bytes. After a failure, discard the reader.

<a id="TarReader.impl"></a>


<a id="TarReader.impl.next"></a>

### Method `next`

```silk
pub fn next(self: &mut TarReader<'a>) -> Result<Option<TarMember<'a>>, TarError>
```

Returns the next member in archive order, or none at the end-of-archive blocks or the end of
the bytes. GNU long-name and pax headers are read as part of the member they name.

#### Errors
- [`TarError`](#TarError) with `Truncated` when the archive ends inside a header or a member,
  `BadHeader` when a checksum or number is invalid, and `UnsafePath` when the member's path
  is absolute, holds a backslash, or has a `..` segment.
